title: PTE Reading: The Five Task Types
summary: Fill in the Blanks, Multiple Choice and Reorder Paragraph — what each asks and where the easy marks are.

chunks.heading: Fill in the Blanks — the reading workhorses
chunks.body: Two versions: **dropdown** (choose the right word from a menu in each gap — this one also feeds your **writing** score) and **drag-and-drop** (drag words from a box into gaps). Both reward **grammar and collocation** sense — which word simply *fits*.
chunks.realExample: Gap: 'a ___ increase in prices' → the options might include 'sharp', 'sharply', 'sharpen'. Grammar picks 'sharp' (adjective before noun). Read the words around the gap, not just the gap.
chunks.memoryHook: The words either side of the blank tell you the answer. Read the collocation.

chunks.heading: Reorder Paragraph — find the opener first
chunks.body: You get jumbled text boxes and **drag them into the logical order**. The trick: **find the sentence that can stand alone as an opener** (no 'this', 'they', 'however' pointing back), then follow the referring words and linkers to chain the rest.
chunks.realExample: A box starting 'However, this later failed…' can never be first — 'However' and 'this' point backward. The opener is usually the one naming the topic in full.
chunks.memoryHook: The opener has no backward-pointing words. Then follow this/these/however like breadcrumbs.

chunks.heading: Multiple Choice — mind the negative marking
chunks.body: **Single answer**: pick the one correct option (safe). **Multiple answers**: select all correct options — but **wrong selections lose marks**, so only tick what you're sure of. Don't select everything hoping to catch them all.
chunks.realExample: On a 'multiple answers' question, picking 3 options where only 2 are right can score the same as picking just the 2 you're confident about — guess-all is a trap.
chunks.memoryHook: Multiple-answer = only tick what you're sure of. Wrong picks bite back.

chunks.heading: Speed and timing
chunks.body: Reading is **section-timed**, not per-question, so **budget your time** and don't sink minutes into one Reorder Paragraph. Answer the quick single-answer and fill-in-blanks items first, then spend leftover time on the fiddly reorder.
chunks.realExample: Stuck on a reorder after 90 seconds? Lock in your best order and move on — an imperfect reorder still earns partial marks for correctly-adjacent pairs.
chunks.memoryHook: Quick wins first. Reorder gives partial marks — never let it eat the clock.

recall.q: Which PTE reading task also contributes to your writing score?
recall.a: Fill in the Blanks (dropdown / 'Reading and Writing: Fill in the Blanks').

recall.q: How do you find the first box in Reorder Paragraph?
recall.a: Find the sentence that stands alone with no backward-pointing words (this, they, however), usually the one naming the topic in full.

recall.q: Why be cautious on 'Multiple Choice, Multiple Answers'?
recall.a: Wrong selections lose marks, so only select the options you're confident are correct.

recall.q: How is the Reading section timed?
recall.a: It's section-timed overall, not per question, so you must budget time across the tasks.

recall.q: What's the fastest way to answer Fill in the Blanks?
recall.a: Read the words on either side of the gap and pick by grammar and collocation — the word that simply fits.
